argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow certification theory. Aggregate readiness passed and deployment guidance supports documented limitations plus active monitoring during rollout, but the exposed public-benefits eligibility segment remains in scope, is below target on residency documentation guidance, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On this record, the defensible position is not that rollout controls cure the weakness; it is that certification can proceed only on a caveated basis tied to explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the known limitation and monitored, reversible rollout.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation beyond a bounded caveat is not required by the current admissible record. A caveated treatment preserves launch velocity better than treating rollout controls as complete governance cover, while still matching the written policy and the known exposed-segment risk. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and reversible rollout reduce the case for broader escalation, but they do not eliminate the disclosure condition.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating a 7% rollout, rollback switch, dashboarding, or monitoring as substitutes for disclosure when the affected named use case remains exposed. The available evidence does support a narrower reading: aggregate readiness and deployment monitoring are relevant to launch management, but policy compliance still turns on disclosing the material limitation before launch unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance, which this record does not show.
concessions: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
That segment is below target on residency documentation guidance.
The available risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not address the public benefits eligibility exposure.
There is no admissible evidence in this record that the required pre-launch disclosure has already been completed or approved.
Rollout controls alone are not enough under the stated policy.
